thread:
Maya Chen: Legal flagged mixed usage of 'retention period' vs 'TTL' in SOC2 audit-log docs. Which to standardize on?
Chris Patel: Use 'retention period' for user-facing docs; keep 'TTL' in infra notes only.
Sara Gomez: Agreed. Legal asked for explicit example numbers and a short exports handling blurb.
Maya Chen: Draft example block: 'Hosted audit logs: 90 days. Privileged access logs: 180 days. Contact support for custom SLAs.'
Liam O'Neil: I'll add minimal SDK snippets for export (curl + python). Use ISO placeholders, no real dates.
Maya Chen: curl snippet:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/exports -d '{"scope":"tenant","before":"YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z"}'
```
Liam O'Neil: python snippet:
```python
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
client.export(scope='tenant', before='YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z')
```
Sara Gomez: Legal provided preferred sentence for exports: 'Exports may include pseudonymized identifiers; customers are responsible for downstream de-identification for regulated workflows.' Use that verbatim.
Chris Patel: Add KMS line: 'Export files are encrypted at rest using customer-managed or Redwood-managed keys; see KMS docs for rotation.'
DocsBot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5401 - linkcheck and build pending.
Maya Chen: Thanks - will incorporate changes and request legal/security sign-off.
